subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should #48874 remain the umbrella RFC for multi-session architecture, or should maintainers supersede it with narrower product-approved trackers for routing, session UI, topic families, and shared memory?
rationale: Current main implements adjacent primitives, but automation cannot safely choose the permanent all-channel session model, new config surface, storage migration, or public-memory privacy boundary.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Work
options.body: Use #48874 for architecture coordination while moving accepted slices into focused session-routing, UI lifecycle, topic-family, and memory/security issues.

options.title: Supersede With Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close this umbrella after designating the narrower open issues and any new missing trackers as canonical for the remaining scope.

options.title: Reject Broad Core Architecture
options.body: Close the RFC as too broad for OpenClaw core unless a concrete missing plugin or session API gap is proven first.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Work
recommendation.body: Use #48874 for architecture coordination while moving accepted slices into focused session-routing, UI lifecycle, topic-family, and memory/security issues.

likelyOwner.reason: They are explicitly cc'd in the RFC, gave canonical-tracker direction on the overlapping WebChat issue, and show recent adjacent routing/session/security history.
